equipment.name: Adjustable Weight Bench
equipment.notes: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER: this bench DOES reach a true DECLINE (head below hips), not incline-only. Decline pressing, decline flyes and decline abdominal work are all performable, with the front leg rollers anchoring the legs. Bench1000 PRO FITNESS. Backrest and seat adjust independently through flat, incline and decline. Leg attachment at the front with padded rollers, used for leg extensions/curls and for securing the legs in decline positions.

equipment.name: Hyperextension bench
equipment.notes: A hyperextension bench or Roman chair. The back pad appears adjustable for height, and the foot rollers are fixed. The angle of the main frame seems to be fixed, providing a decline angle.
A black flat weight bench with a black upholstered pad. The brand "CAP" is visible on the side of the pad. It appears to be in good condition. The bench has a stable H-shaped base.
equipment.name: Flat weight bench

equipment.notes: A pair of yellow parallel dip bars with black foam grips. They appear to be fixed height and stable, suitable for bodyweight exercises.
equipment.name: Parallel dip bars

equipment.notes: Pair of adjustable dumbbells, TRULAP, 8.5 lb to 92 lb per hand. TWO HARD LIMITS, confirmed by the owner: (1) the handles are ROUND-BODIED and ROLL under load — they are NOT a stable base for any bodyweight movement, so never prescribe push-ups, planks, renegade rows or any hold that puts bodyweight through them; (2) 8.5 lb is the LOWEST notch, which is too heavy for light prehab work — rotator-cuff external rotation, scaption, W-raises and similar belong on bands, not on these.
equipment.name: Adjustable dumbbells on stand

exercises.name: Leg Extension (seated)
exercises.how: Sit on the bench, hook feet under pad. Extend legs fully, squeezing quadriceps at the top. Lower with control.
Lie face down on the bench, hook heels under pad. Curl legs towards glutes, squeezing hamstrings. Lower with control.
exercises.auditReason: Equipment vs movement: the bench's leg attachment is described for leg extension, and a prone curl needs the roller reachable at ankle height while lying face down — needs a human to confirm the attachment supports the prone position.
exercises.name: Leg Curl (prone)

exercises.how: Lie on the decline bench, hook feet under pads. Place hands behind head or across chest. Crunch upwards, lifting shoulders off the bench without pulling on the neck.
exercises.name: Crunches (decline)

exercises.how: Sit on the edge of the bench, hands beside hips, fingers gripping the edge. Slide hips forward off the bench and lower body by bending elbows. Keep elbows pointing straight back.
exercises.name: Bench Dips

exercises.how: Place hands on the bench, wider than shoulder-width apart. Maintain a straight line from head to heels. Lower chest towards the bench, then push back up.
exercises.name: Incline Push-ups

exercises.how: Stand tall, light dumbbells at your sides, raise them out to shoulder height with a slight elbow bend. Lead with the elbows, stop at shoulder level, lower slowly.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise

exercises.how: Light dumbbells in front of your thighs, lift straight arms to eye level one at a time or together. Keep ribs down so you don't lean back.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Raise

exercises.how: Sit, rest forearms on your thighs or the bench with palms up and wrists past the edge. Curl the weight up with the hand only, no forearm movement.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
exercises.how: Same seated position but palms down, wrists off the knee or bench edge. Lift the back of the hand up, go light, control the way down.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
exercises.how: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, curl up without swinging the elbows forward. Keep elbows pinned to your ribs the whole way.
Curl with palms facing each other, thumbs up, elbows tight to your sides. Don't let the shoulders shrug up at the top.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.how: Set the backrest around 45 degrees, sit back with arms hanging straight down, curl up. Keep your upper arms behind your torso and shoulders pressed into the pad.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.how: Sit on the bench, elbow braced against the inside of your thigh, curl one dumbbell up. No body English — only the forearm moves.

exercises.name: Zottman Curl
exercises.how: Curl up palms-up, rotate to palms-down at the top, lower slowly in that position. Go lighter than a normal curl — the lowering is the work.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
exercises.how: One hand and knee on the bench, upper arm parallel to the floor, straighten the elbow behind you. Keep the back flat and the upper arm still.

exercises.name: Lying Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.how: Lie on the bench, dumbbells above your chest, bend at the elbows to lower them beside your head. Keep the upper arms vertical and don't flare the elbows wide.

exercises.auditReason: RISK borderline: the bottom position is a loaded overhead stretch, so shoulder could justify 'high' for an athlete with any shoulder history; back:moderate reflects the lumbar-extension tendency even with the pad.
exercises.name: Seated Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.how: Sit with the backrest upright, hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands, lower it behind your head and press back up. Back stays against the pad, ribs down.
Lie on the bench, dumbbells touching each other over your chest, press straight up keeping them pressed together. Elbows stay tucked close to your ribs.
exercises.name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Press
Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.how: Lie flat, dumbbells at chest level, press up until arms are straight over your chest. Keep both feet planted and don't arch the lower back off the bench.
Set the backrest to 30-45 degrees, press the dumbbells from upper-chest level to straight overhead. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.
exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.how: Set the bench to decline and hook your legs under the padded rollers, press the dumbbells from lower chest to lockout. Sit up slowly between sets, don't jerk upright.
Lie flat, arms wide with a soft elbow bend, open out until you feel a chest stretch then hug back together. Stop the stretch at chest level — don't drop the elbows below the bench.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Fly
exercises.auditReason: Single-joint horizontal adduction so tagged 'isolation' per the rule, but for recovery tracking it loads the same tissue as 'push' — a human should confirm which the recovery model expects.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
exercises.auditReason: Movement is single-joint shoulder adduction, so pattern is tagged isolation rather than push; shoulder set to moderate because the bottom position is loaded end-range horizontal abduction.
exercises.how: Backrest at 30-45 degrees, arms wide with soft elbows, open and hug back together over the upper chest. Keep the weight light and the movement slow.
Lie along the bench holding one dumbbell over your chest, lower it back over your head with slightly bent arms, pull it back. Keep ribs pulled down so the lower back stays flat.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover
Push-up on Dumbbells
exercises.how: Set two dumbbells on the floor shoulder-width and grip them like handles, then push up with a deeper chest drop. Squeeze the glutes so the hips don't sag.
exercises.auditReason: the TRULAP dumbbells are round-bodied and roll under load — not a handle base

exercises.how: Feet up on the bench, hands on the floor, lower your chest to the floor and press back. Keep a straight line from heels to head, don't let the hips drop.
exercises.name: Decline Push-up
Dips
exercises.how: Support yourself on the bars, lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, press back up. Stop at parallel — going deeper strains the shoulder.
Start at the top of the bars with arms locked and lower yourself over 4-5 seconds, then step off and reset. Keep the shoulders down away from your ears.
exercises.name: Negative Dips
exercises.auditReason: Eccentric-only work progresses by variation (slower tempo, then full dips), so progressionMode is difficulty, not reps or duration.

exercises.how: One hand and same-side knee on the bench, row the dumbbell to your hip. Keep the back flat and square — no twisting the torso to lift it.
exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row

exercises.how: Set the backrest to about 45 degrees and lie face-down on it, row both dumbbells to your ribs. Chest stays glued to the pad the whole set.
exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row

exercises.auditReason: primaryRole set to prehab rather than strength — intensity 1 at 3x20 is rear-delt/scapular health work that should not be loaded and progressed like a row.
exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Reverse Fly
exercises.how: Face-down on the incline bench, light dumbbells hanging, sweep the arms out and back like opening wings. Squeeze the shoulder blades, don't shrug.
Face-down on the incline bench with very light dumbbells, raise the arms overhead into a Y shape. Thumbs up, no shrugging, tiny weight only.
exercises.name: Prone Dumbbell Y-Raise

exercises.auditReason: Same as the chest-supported version: single-joint rear-delt accessory tagged shoulder/prehab so it is not progressed like a strength lift.
exercises.how: Sit on the bench edge, lean your chest onto your thighs, sweep light dumbbells out to the sides. Chest stays on the thighs so the back never works.
exercises.name: Seated Bent-Over Dumbbell Reverse Fly

exercises.how: Hinge to about 45 degrees with a flat back, row both dumbbells to your ribs. Brace hard and stop the set the moment the back rounds.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row

exercises.auditReason: round adjustable dumbbells roll under a plank; band Pallof + bird dog row + suitcase hold cover anti-rotation better
exercises.how: Push-up position gripping two dumbbells, feet wide, row one dumbbell up while the hips stay perfectly still. If the hips rotate, go lighter.
exercises.name: Renegade Row

exercises.how: Stand with heavy dumbbells at your sides and lift the shoulders straight up toward your ears, then lower fully. Don't roll the shoulders, straight up and down.
exercises.auditReason: Single-joint scapular elevation, so pattern is isolation rather than pull; back set to moderate because heavy dumbbells are held in standing spinal compression.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug

exercises.how: Hips on the pad, ankles under the rollers, lower your torso then lift until your body is a straight line. Stop at straight — don't arch past it.
exercises.name: Back Extension

exercises.how: Get into the back-extension position and hold your torso level with the floor, arms crossed on your chest. Breathe normally; stop when the hips start sagging.
exercises.name: Sorensen Hold

exercises.how: Lie face-down with hips on the pad and hold the frame, then lift your straight legs up to body level. Move slowly with the glutes, no swinging.
exercises.name: Reverse Hyperextension
Weighted Back Extension
exercises.how: Hold a dumbbell to your chest and perform back extensions, stopping when your body is straight. Never bounce at the bottom.
Backrest fully upright, sit with your back flat against it, press dumbbells from shoulder height to overhead. Keep the back on the pad — no leaning back to push.
exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press

exercises.how: Sit with the backrest upright, start with palms facing you at chin height, rotate the palms forward as you press up. Back stays flat on the pad.
exercises.name: Seated Arnold Press

exercises.auditReason: Real and correctly described, but loaded abduction with internal rotation is a poor fit for a 43-year-old pickleball player who needs durable shoulders.
exercises.how: Pull the dumbbells up the front of your body to chest height, elbows leading. Stop at chest height — higher pinches the shoulder.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Upright Row
Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
exercises.how: Lie on your side on the bench, elbow tucked at your ribs at 90 degrees, rotate a very light dumbbell up. Elbow never leaves your side.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.how: Hold one dumbbell vertically at your chest, squat down between your knees and stand up. Elbows inside the knees, chest up, weight stays close to the body.

exercises.auditReason: Dumbbell hangs between the legs so range is capped by arm length before depth; workable but the load path differs from the goblet version and a human should confirm intensity 2 at 3x15 is the intent.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
exercises.how: Feet wide, toes out, hold one dumbbell hanging between your legs and squat straight down. Knees track over the toes, torso stays tall.
Rear foot on the bench, dumbbells at your sides, drop the back knee straight down and drive up through the front heel. Keep the front shin near vertical and the torso tall.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
Dumbbell Step-up
exercises.how: Dumbbells at your sides, step one foot onto the bench and stand up fully without pushing off the back leg. Lower under control, don't drop down.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.how: Hold dumbbells at your sides, step back and drop the rear knee toward the floor, then drive forward to stand. Stepping backwards keeps the front knee calm.
Hold one dumbbell at your chest, step wide to one side and sit back into that hip while the other leg stays straight. Keep both feet flat and the chest up.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Lunge
Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.auditReason: Pattern is arguable — hip extension makes it a hinge, but some catalogs file glute bridges under core/isolation; flagging so the human can settle the convention.

demo.sourceName: single leg bridge with outstretched leg

exercises.how: Lie on your back, one foot planted and the other leg straight up, push the hips up level. Keep the hips square — don't let one side drop.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.how: Dumbbells in front of your thighs, push the hips back and slide the weights down your legs with a flat back, then stand. Stop when the hamstrings tighten, never round the back.

exercises.auditReason: Listed bodyweight with balance as the point, so progression is difficulty rather than load; if the catalog intends it to become a loaded single-leg RDL the mode and equipment both need changing.
exercises.how: Stand on one leg, hinge forward reaching toward the floor as the free leg lifts behind you. Keep hips level and back flat; balance is the point, not load.
exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift

exercises.auditReason: Equipment vs setup: the leg-extension rollers sit at seated height on the bench front, so kneeling on the floor with ankles locked under them may not be geometrically possible or stable.
exercises.how: Kneel with ankles locked under the bench's padded rollers, lower your torso forward as slowly as you can, then push off with your hands. Keep hips extended in a straight line, don't bend at the waist.
exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl

exercises.how: Hold yourself up on the dip bars with arms locked, then raise the knees toward your chest. Move slowly and don't swing — the swing is what tugs the lower back.
exercises.name: Dip Bar Support Knee Raise

exercises.how: Support on the bars with arms straight, lift both legs out in front until they're level with your hips. Press the shoulders down; bend the knees if you can't hold it straight.
exercises.name: L-Sit Hold

exercises.how: Hold yourself at the top of the dip bars with elbows locked and shoulders pushed down away from your ears. Squeeze glutes and abs so you don't hang loose.
exercises.name: Parallel Bar Support Hold

exercises.how: Lie on the bench holding the edge behind your head, raise straight legs to vertical then lower slowly. Stop lowering the moment your lower back lifts off the bench.
exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
exercises.auditReason: Back risk raised to moderate: straight-leg raises load lumbar extension via the hip flexors, which matters given the lower-back-resilience priority — a human should confirm moderate rather than low.

exercises.how: Lie on your back, knees bent over your hips, curl the pelvis up to lift the hips a few inches. Small controlled movement — no throwing the legs.
exercises.name: Reverse Crunch

exercises.how: Lie on your back, hands under your hips, legs straight and a few inches off the floor, alternate small kicks. Press the lower back into the floor the whole time.
exercises.auditReason: Sustained straight-leg hip-flexor load pulls on the lumbar spine, so back is moderate rather than low for an athlete whose top priority is lower-back resilience.
exercises.name: Flutter Kicks
Hollow Body Rock
exercises.how: Hold the hollow position — arms overhead, legs straight, low back pressed down — and rock gently back and forth. If the back lifts, tuck the knees in.
exercises.auditReason: Timed hold makes duration correct, but the rocking version is itself a difficulty step above the static hollow hold, so the catalog may intend difficulty — worth a human check.
Correct as data, but repeated unloaded flexion-plus-rotation is a weak fit for an athlete whose stated priority is lower-back resilience and anti-rotation strength.
exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.how: On your back, alternate bringing opposite elbow and knee together while the other leg extends. Rotate from the ribs, don't yank on your neck.
In a high plank with feet wide, tap one hand to the opposite shoulder and swap. The hips must not rock — slow it down until they stay still.
exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Tap

exercises.how: Forearms on the floor, feet up on the bench, hold a straight line from heels to head. Tuck the ribs and squeeze the glutes so the hips don't sag.
exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Plank

exercises.auditReason: Prescription is timed so progressionMode could read as duration, but the knee-to-straight-leg regression ladder is the real driver, so difficulty is tagged; bottom shoulder carries body weight, hence shoulder moderate.
exercises.how: Side plank on your forearm with the top leg's inner knee or ankle resting on the bench, lift the hips. Start with the knee version; keep the body in one line.
exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank

exercises.how: Hold one heavy dumbbell in one hand and walk slowly, staying perfectly upright. Do not lean away from the weight — the fight to stay level is the exercise.
exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
Farmer's Walk
exercises.how: A dumbbell in each hand, walk tall with the shoulders back and short quick steps. Stop when your posture breaks, not when your grip does.

exercises.name: Decline Sit-up
exercises.how: Legs hooked under the padded rollers on the decline bench, sit all the way up and lower under control. Don't drop back fast or pull on your neck.
exercises.auditReason: Real and correctly described, but full-range decline sit-ups are repeated end-range spinal flexion under torso load, a poor fit for an athlete whose top priority is lower-back resilience; back risk set to high accordingly.

exercises.how: Sit leaning back with feet off the floor and rotate your torso side to side. Rotate from the ribs and keep the chest tall.
exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.auditReason: Accurately described, but repeated lumbar rotation in a flexed seated position works against the lower-back resilience goal; anti-rotation work would serve the athlete better.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Side Bend
exercises.auditReason: Correctly described, but loaded lateral spinal flexion is a poor fit for a lower-back-priority athlete; flagged back:high accordingly.
exercises.how: One dumbbell in one hand, bend sideways at the waist then pull back up with the obliques. Move only side to side, never twisting.

exercises.name: Skater Jumps
exercises.how: Bound sideways from one foot to the other, landing softly on a bent knee and holding the balance for a beat. Land quietly — noise means you're landing stiff.

exercises.name: Squat Jump
exercises.how: Drop into a shallow squat and jump as high as you can, landing soft with bent knees. Absorb every landing — no stiff legs.

exercises.name: Push-ups
exercises.how: Hands under the shoulders, body in one straight line, chest to just above the floor.
Hands on a bench or step. Easier than the floor — perfect as a ramp-in set.
exercises.name: Incline push-ups

exercises.how: Hang, pull until your chin clears the bar, lower all the way down under control.
exercises.name: Pull-ups

exercises.how: On your back, lower back glued to the floor. Extend opposite arm and leg slowly, then swap.
exercises.name: Dead bug

exercises.auditReason: Primary demand is anti-extension trunk control in a plank, so core/stability is tagged rather than push; the fast tempo means it also functions as conditioning, which this taxonomy has no slot for.
exercises.how: Push-up position, drive the knees to the chest fast without the hips bouncing.
exercises.name: Mountain climbers
Bear crawl
exercises.how: On hands and toes, knees an inch off the floor, crawl forward and back staying low.
exercises.auditReason: Pattern is defensible as either core (anti-extension/anti-rotation quadrupedal control) or carry (loaded locomotion); tagged core because the trunk demand dominates and no external load is carried.

exercises.name: Alternating lunges
exercises.how: Step forward, back knee towards the floor, push back to the start. Alternate legs.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
exercises.how: On your back, heels close to the hips, drive through the heels and squeeze at the top.
Forearms down, body in one line, ribs pulled down, squeeze everything. Hold.
exercises.name: Plank
Side plank
exercises.how: On one forearm, hips stacked and lifted, body in a straight line. Both sides.

exercises.name: Calf raises
exercises.how: Up on the toes as high as you can, slow all the way back down.
Hands on a chair edge behind you, elbows straight back, lower until the elbows hit 90°.
exercises.name: Bench Dips
exercises.auditReason: Equipment vs description: the row lists the flat bench but the instructions say 'chair edge', and the loaded end-range shoulder extension is a bad match for a pickleball player's shoulders.

exercises.how: Hips high in an upside-down V, lower the crown of the head towards the floor.
exercises.name: Pike push-ups
exercises.auditReason: Pattern could legitimately be tagged shoulder rather than push since the press is vertical/overhead; tagged push because the taxonomy's shoulder slot reads as prehab-style shoulder work, and the overhead-ish loading justifies shoulder:moderate.

exercises.name: Jumping jacks
exercises.how: Classic. Feet out, arms up, keep the rhythm.
Arms out, small fast circles forward then backward. Great as a first move.
exercises.name: Arm circles
Wall sit
exercises.how: Back flat on the wall, thighs parallel to the floor. Sit there and suffer politely.
Feet shoulder width, sit back and down, knees tracking over the toes, stand tall.
exercises.name: Bodyweight squats
Superman hold
exercises.how: Face down, lift chest, arms and legs, look at the floor. Hold and breathe.
On all fours, extend opposite arm and leg, hold a beat, keep the hips level. Gold for the lower back.
exercises.auditReason: Movement and pattern match, but progression is by variation (longer levers, added hold), not by the 16 reps listed, so the rep count is decorative.
exercises.name: Bird dog
Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.how: Lie on the floor, knees bent, press dumbbells from chest to lockout. Let the upper arms rest on the floor briefly at the bottom.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.how: Lie on the floor and press one dumbbell while the other arm stays flat. Brace hard so your ribs do not twist off the floor.
exercises.auditReason: Tagged push because the joint action is a press; the strong anti-rotation demand described in the cue is not captured by a single pattern field.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
exercises.how: Lie on the bench, press two dumbbells held tight together, crushing them inward the whole rep. Keep elbows tucked and shoulders on the pad.

exercises.name: Low-Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.how: Set the backrest to the lowest incline notch and press dumbbells over the upper chest. Keep the lower back flat on the pad, no arching.

exercises.auditReason: Setup and tags check out; shoulder set to moderate because the wide straight-arm arc reaches end-range with load even though the prescribed weight is light.
exercises.how: Lie on the bench with light dumbbells at your hips, sweep them in a wide arc overhead and back. Keep arms nearly straight and move slowly.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Around the World
Svend Press
exercises.how: Stand and squeeze the medicine ball between both palms at chest height, then press it straight out and back. Keep squeezing the whole time.
exercises.auditReason: Load vs purpose: only one 10lb medicine ball exists, so the load-based progression has nowhere to go, and a round ball squeezes differently from the flat plates the movement is defined by.

exercises.how: One hand on the medicine ball, one on the floor, do a push-up keeping hips square. Swap hands each set.
exercises.name: Medicine Ball Push-up
exercises.auditReason: Workable, but a 10lb medicine ball is unstable under a loaded hand; wrist and shoulder demand is higher than the intensity-2 rating suggests.

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Push-up
exercises.how: Feet on the bench, hands on the floor, lower your chest to the floor. Squeeze glutes so hips do not sag.
Hands wide, lower toward one hand while the other arm straightens out sideways. Keep hips level and do not let the straight arm collapse.
exercises.name: Archer Push-up
exercises.auditReason: Progression is by variation toward one-arm work rather than by reps; the extended arm also sits in a wide, loaded position that warrants at least moderate shoulder risk.

exercises.name: Knee Push-up
exercises.how: Push-up from the knees with a straight line from knees to head. Keep the belly tight so the back does not sag.

exercises.auditReason: Correct as a power/quality entry, but the hand landing is a hard impact on wrist and shoulder, so shoulder is set high and this should be gated for the 12-year-old.
exercises.name: Plyometric Push-up
exercises.how: Lower into a push-up then push hard enough that your hands leave the floor. Land with soft elbows.
Hands wider than shoulders, lower until the chest is just off the floor. Keep elbows around 45 degrees, not flared to 90.
exercises.name: Wide-Grip Push-up

exercises.how: Hands together forming a diamond under the chest, lower and press. Keep elbows brushing your ribs.
exercises.name: Diamond Push-up
Push-up to Downward Dog
exercises.how: Do a push-up, then push your hips up and back into a downward dog before returning. Move continuously and breathe out on each push.
exercises.auditReason: Treated as a warm-up flow (mobility / none) rather than a push strength exercise, since the push-up here is a transition rather than the trained element.

exercises.how: Lie on the bench, palms facing each other, press the dumbbells up and together. Keep elbows tucked close to the ribs.
exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Bench Press

exercises.how: Set the bench to decline, secure your legs in the rollers, and open the dumbbells wide with a slight elbow bend. Stop when your hands reach chest level.
exercises.auditReason: Setup and movement are valid on this decline-capable bench; pattern is ambiguous between push and isolation — tagged isolation because the fly is single-joint shoulder adduction with no elbow extension.
exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Fly

exercises.how: Hands on the bars, feet on the floor behind you in a push-up plank, lower your chest between the bars. Keep the body in one straight line.
exercises.name: Dip Bar Push-up

exercises.how: Support yourself on the bars with a forward lean and lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor. Stop if your shoulders roll forward.
exercises.name: Parallel Bar Dip

exercises.how: Hands on the dip bars, heels on the bench in front so your legs take part of the weight. Lower slowly and press back up.
exercises.name: Feet-Supported Dip
Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
exercises.how: Chest on the incline bench, row the dumbbells with elbows flared wide out to the sides. Keep your chest glued to the pad.

exercises.name: Seal Row
exercises.auditReason: Equipment vs setup: a seal row needs the bench elevated so the dumbbells clear the floor at full extension, and a standard flat CAP bench is too low for that without blocks.
exercises.how: Lie face down along the bench with dumbbells hanging, row them to your ribs. Do not lift your chest off the pad to cheat.
One hand and one knee on the bench, row the kettlebell to your hip. Keep your spine flat and square, no twisting.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Single-Arm Row

exercises.how: Lie under one dip bar, grip it, and pull your chest to the bar with heels on the floor. Keep hips lifted in a straight line.
exercises.auditReason: Movement, pattern and tags all match; only uncertainty is whether the fixed-height dip bars sit high enough for a heels-on-floor row.
exercises.name: Inverted Row

exercises.auditReason: Equipment-vs-movement: feet on a bench requires the fixed-height dip bar to clear bench height plus torso thickness, which is unverified for these bars.
exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Inverted Row
exercises.how: Under the dip bar with your feet up on the bench, pull your chest to the bar. Keep the body rigid from heels to head.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Prone T-Raise
exercises.how: Chest on the incline bench, raise light dumbbells straight out to the sides into a T. Lead with the thumbs and squeeze the shoulder blades.
Chest on the incline bench, pull light dumbbells back with bent elbows into a W shape. Move slowly, no swinging.
exercises.auditReason: Load-vs-purpose: the how-to says 'light dumbbells' but the lightest available load is 8 lb per hand, far above the 2–5 lb typical for prone scapular/cuff W-raises.
exercises.name: Prone Dumbbell W-Raise

exercises.auditReason: Movement is scapular depression/retraction in a hang, so it sits between 'pull' and 'shoulder'; tagged shoulder/prehab so it is not loaded and progressed like a real pull-up.
exercises.name: Scapular Pull-up
exercises.how: Hang from the bar with straight arms and pull your shoulder blades down without bending the elbows. Small range, slow tempo.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.how: Hang from the bar with relaxed shoulders and straight arms for time. Breathe steadily; drop before your grip fails suddenly.

Step up to the top of the pull-up from a bench or box — do not jump. Lower yourself as slowly as you can, aiming for five seconds down. Progress by slowing the descent, then by graduating to a full pull-up.
exercises.name: Negative Pull-up

exercises.how: Hang with palms facing you, pull until your chin clears the bar. Keep ribs down so you do not arch the lower back.
exercises.name: Chin-up

exercises.auditReason: as written it is an upright row, not a high pull; the position is also an impingement risk
exercises.how: From hip height, pull light dumbbells up to chest level with elbows leading high. Stay upright, no back swing.
exercises.name: Dumbbell High Pull
Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.how: Sit tall on the bench with the backrest up and raise dumbbells to shoulder height. Sitting stops you swinging with your back.
Seated with back support: upright row to elbow height, rotate the light dumbbells up, then press. Go light and slow.
exercises.auditReason: Load-vs-purpose: the defining rotation phase is end-range external rotation and the 8 lb minimum dumbbell is too heavy for it, which is also why shoulder risk is high.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Cuban Press

exercises.how: Sit on the bench edge, chest on thighs, raise light dumbbells out to the sides. Keep your chest resting on your legs the whole set.
exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise

exercises.auditReason: Load-vs-purpose: prescribed as light prehab at 3×15 but 8 lb per hand is the floor, which is borderline heavy for scaption in a cuff-health role.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Scaption Raise
exercises.how: Raise light dumbbells up at a 45-degree angle between front and side, thumbs up. Stop at shoulder height.

exercises.name: Wall Handstand Hold
exercises.how: Walk your feet up the wall until your chest faces it, hold with straight arms. Come down as soon as your arms shake.

exercises.name: Crab Walk
exercises.how: Sit with hands behind you, lift your hips and walk forward and back on hands and feet. Keep hips high the whole way.
exercises.auditReason: movementPattern is genuinely ambiguous — it is loaded quadrupedal locomotion, so 'core' or 'carry' both defend, and the shoulder sits in loaded extension which I rated moderate rather than low.

exercises.name: Inchworm
exercises.how: From standing, hinge down, walk your hands out to a plank, then walk your feet in. Bend the knees rather than rounding the back.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
exercises.how: Hold the kettlebell at your chest by the horns and squat between your knees. Keep your chest tall and elbows inside the knees.
exercises.auditReason: progressionMode 'load' is correct for the exercise but unachievable with the inventory — there is exactly one 37.5lb kettlebell, so load cannot actually increase; consider swapping the implement to a dumbbell or accepting reps.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Suitcase Deadlift
exercises.how: Kettlebell beside one foot, hinge and stand up with it like a suitcase. Keep both shoulders level and the spine neutral.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
exercises.how: Feet staggered, dumbbells at your sides, drop the back knee toward the floor. Keep the front shin near vertical.

exercises.auditReason: riskProfiles.knee is a judgment call — the crossed-behind stance loads the front knee in adduction/valgus under dumbbells, which for a 43-year-old pickleball player sits at the moderate/high boundary, and the 12-year-old should probably not load it at all.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Curtsy Lunge
exercises.how: Step one leg diagonally behind the other and lower. Keep hips facing forward and do not twist the torso.

exercises.auditReason: laterality is alternating rather than left-then-right, so it is tagged 'unilateral' not 'perSide'; also 3×20 walking steps needs clear floor length that a home gym may not have.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
exercises.how: Hold dumbbells at your sides and lunge forward step by step. Keep the torso upright, knee tracking over the toes.

exercises.name: Bench Hip Thrust
exercises.how: Upper back on the bench, dumbbell across the hips, drive hips up to a straight line. Tuck the chin and squeeze glutes at the top, no back arch.
Lie on the floor with heels on the bench, drive hips up. Squeeze glutes at the top rather than arching the lower back.
exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Glute Bridge

demo.sourceName: glute bridge two legs on bench (male)

exercises.how: Step up onto the bench with one foot, stand tall, step down with control. Drive through the heel of the top foot.
exercises.name: Bench Step-up
exercises.auditReason: equipment fit is borderline: the CAP flat bench has an H-base and an upholstered pad, so single-leg step-ups load it off-center on a soft, tippable surface — usable but worth a human confirming the bench is stable under offset load.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.how: Jump onto the bench with both feet and land softly in a quarter squat. Step down, never jump down.
exercises.auditReason: Equipment-vs-movement: no plyo box exists and a flat CAP bench is not a stable jump surface, and 3×8 is a volume prescription for a quality-terminated jump in a 43-year-old.

exercises.name: Split Squat Jump
exercises.how: From a split stance, jump and switch legs in the air, landing softly. Three per side. Stop the set the moment jump height, landing control or speed drops — even at two reps. Full rest between sets; never take this near failure.

exercises.name: Wall Sit with Medicine Ball Squeeze
exercises.how: Wall sit at 90 degrees with the medicine ball squeezed between your knees. Keep the whole back flat against the wall.
Stand on one foot holding a dumbbell, rise onto the ball of the foot and lower slowly. Hold something for balance if needed.
exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise

exercises.how: Kettlebell between your feet, hinge at the hips and stand up. Keep the back flat and the bell close to your shins.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Deadlift

exercises.auditReason: movementPattern is contestable — the swing is a ballistic hinge, and tagging it 'hinge' vs 'power' changes which recovery slot it consumes; I chose 'hinge' because the posterior-chain fatigue is what matters for the athlete's lower-back priority, with primaryRole carrying the power intent.
exercises.how: Hinge and hike the bell back, then snap the hips to float it to chest height. Arms stay relaxed, the hips do the work.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
Kettlebell Halo
exercises.auditReason: Load-vs-purpose: the only kettlebell is 37.5 lb, well above the 10–20 lb range that keeps a halo a shoulder-mobility drill rather than a loaded overhead challenge.
exercises.how: Hold the bell upside down at chest height and circle it slowly around your head. Keep ribs down and hips still.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Around the Body Pass
exercises.how: Pass the kettlebell around your waist from hand to hand. Keep hips and shoulders square, only the arms move.
exercises.auditReason: Correctly described anti-rotation warm-up; pattern could arguably be anti-rotation rather than core, and 37.5 lb is heavy but workable for a pass.
progressionMode 'load' cannot be executed — one fixed 37.5lb bell means the only path is reps; a dumbbell version would make the tag honest.
exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Kettlebell Press
exercises.how: One knee down, press the kettlebell overhead. Squeeze the down-side glute so the lower back does not arch.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Goblet Hold
exercises.how: Hold the kettlebell at your chest and stand tall for time. Ribs down, breathe through the brace.
Kettlebell racked on one shoulder, step back into a lunge. Stay upright and resist leaning toward the loaded side.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Front Rack Reverse Lunge

demo.sourceName: Fitness Workout GIF by ATH Sport

exercises.auditReason: Load-vs-purpose: the single 37.5 lb bell is the entry load with no lighter option, which is a heavy first get-up and drives shoulder risk to high under a long overhead lockout.
exercises.name: Turkish Get-up
exercises.how: From lying, stand up step by step keeping the bell locked overhead, then reverse it. Eyes on the bell the whole time.
Lift the ball overhead and slam it down hard, catching the bounce. Hinge at the hips, do not round the back to reach it.
exercises.auditReason: a 10 lb ball is not a dead-bounce slam ball, and 12 reps of loaded overhead-to-floor flexion fights the lower-back goal
exercises.name: Medicine Ball Slam

exercises.auditReason: Row is stored as a weight/load-style entry with 3×6 prescription, but the how-to correctly terminates the set on speed drop — the metadata (progression/measure) contradicts the described quality-based throw, so the load/rep framing needs a human fix.
exercises.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
exercises.how: Stand facing a wall, ball at the chest. Drive it into the wall as hard as you can and catch the rebound. Stop the set the moment the throw slows — even at two reps. Full rest between sets.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Dead Bug
exercises.how: Lie on your back holding the ball, press it against your knees while lowering the opposite arm and leg. Keep the lower back pressed flat.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Plank Roll
exercises.how: In a plank, roll the ball from one hand to the other under your chest. Hips stay level, no rocking.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball V-Sit Hold
exercises.how: Balance on your sit bones holding the ball out in front, legs off the floor. Keep the chest up rather than rounding.

exercises.auditReason: movementPattern is a judgement call: the isometric is a squat hold but the prescribed work (passing the ball around the knees) is trunk/anti-rotation, so a human should confirm which slot it should fill.
exercises.how: Hold a wall sit while passing the ball hand to hand around your knees. Keep hips at knee height the whole time.
exercises.name: Medicine Ball Wall Sit Pass

exercises.how: Hold the ball overhead and sit into a squat, holding the bottom position. Keep arms locked and the chest tall.
exercises.name: Medicine Ball Overhead Squat Hold
exercises.auditReason: end-range overhead flexion plus a deep loaded bottom position held for time

exercises.name: Bench Plank
exercises.how: Forearms on the bench, feet on the floor, hold a straight line. Squeeze glutes so hips do not drop.
Half-kneeling, hold a light dumbbell at your chest with both hands and press it straight out. Resist any twist as the arms extend.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Pallof Press
exercises.auditReason: equipment vs movement: a Pallof press is defined by resistance anchored to the side of the body, and a dumbbell held at the chest applies no lateral force, so with no cable or bands available this exercise cannot exist here.

exercises.how: On all fours with one leg extended back, row a light dumbbell with the opposite arm. Keep hips square to the floor.
exercises.auditReason: primaryRole is a judgement call: loading is limited by the anti-rotation demand rather than by the lats, so it behaves as stability work even though the pattern is a pull.
exercises.name: Bird Dog Row

exercises.how: Hang from the bar and raise both knees to your chest. Move slowly, no swinging between reps.
exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
Side Plank with Leg Raise
exercises.how: Hold a side plank and lift the top leg up and down. Keep hips stacked and lifted.

exercises.name: Plank to Push-up
exercises.auditReason: movementPattern is contestable: the up-down is anti-rotation/core dominant rather than a true press, so tagging it 'push' would corrupt push-day recovery tracking — a human should confirm the core tag.
exercises.how: From a forearm plank, press up to your hands one arm at a time, then back down. Minimise hip sway.

exercises.name: Bench Knee Tuck
exercises.how: Sit on the bench, hands gripping behind you, lean back slightly and pull your knees to your chest. Keep the chest tall, do not round hard.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.how: Lie on your back, lift shoulders and legs, arms overhead. Press the lower back into the floor; raise the legs higher if it lifts.

exercises.name: Hip Dip Side Plank
exercises.how: In a side plank, lower the hip toward the floor and drive it back up. Keep the shoulder stacked over the elbow.
Lie face down, lift chest and arms with thumbs up, squeezing the shoulder blades. Keep the neck long, eyes on the floor.
exercises.name: Prone Cobra
Hyperextension Bench Side Bend
exercises.auditReason: Equipment-vs-movement: the Roman chair has fixed foot rollers and a fixed decline frame built for prone hip hinging, so side-lying anchoring is questionable, and repeated unsupported lateral spinal flexion conflicts with a lower-back-resilience priority.
exercises.how: Lie sideways on the hyperextension pad with feet locked, lower and raise your torso to the side. Small range, no twisting.
On the hyperextension bench with one foot behind the roller, raise to a straight line only. Never arch past neutral.
exercises.name: Single-Leg Back Extension

exercises.how: Set up on the hyperextension bench and hold your torso level with the floor. Squeeze glutes and keep the chin tucked.
exercises.name: Hyperextension Isometric Hold
Decline Bench Reverse Crunch
exercises.auditReason: Equipment-vs-setup: the movement requires lying reversed on the bench (head at the high end) and gripping the front leg rollers behind the head for anchorage, which is the opposite orientation to this bench's decline configuration and may not be usable or stable as described.
exercises.how: Lie head-up on the declined bench gripping behind your head, curl the knees toward your chest. Lift with the abs, not momentum.
Cradle a dumbbell in the crooks of both elbows and squat. Keep the chest up; stop the set the moment the back rounds.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Zercher Squat
exercises.auditReason: a Zercher needs a bar spanning both elbow crooks; this is a goblet squat, which already exists twice

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise
exercises.how: Sit on the bench with dumbbells on your knees and drive up onto your toes. Pause at the top of each rep.

exercises.auditReason: bodyweight held through round dumbbell handles that roll — the owner confirms they are not a stable base
exercises.how: Hold the bottom of a push-up on the dumbbell handles with your chest just off the floor. Keep elbows tucked and hips level.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Push-up Isometric Hold
Reverse Plank
exercises.how: Sit with hands behind you, lift hips until the body is a straight line, heels on the floor. Look forward, not back.

exercises.name: Frog Jump
exercises.how: Squat down, touch the floor, jump forward and land back in a squat. Land softly with knees tracking over the toes.

exercises.auditReason: Real and correctly described, but deep sustained knee flexion serves none of this athlete's stated priorities and carries high knee load at 43.
exercises.how: Stay in a low squat and walk forward in small steps. Keep the chest up and heels down as much as you can.
exercises.name: Duck Walk
Lateral Bear Crawl
exercises.auditReason: Pattern is defensible as 'lateral' for the frontal-plane locomotion, but the dominant training effect is anti-rotation trunk control — a human should confirm which slot it should fill.
exercises.how: On hands and toes with knees just off the floor, crawl sideways. Keep hips low and level, no bouncing.

exercises.auditReason: At bodyweight intensity 2 this sits between mobility and strength; primaryRole 'mobility' with progressionMode 'none' would be equally defensible.
exercises.how: Feet wide, shift your weight onto one bent leg keeping the other straight. Keep the heel of the working leg down and chest tall.
exercises.name: Cossack Squat
90/90 Hip Switch
exercises.how: Sit with both knees bent at 90 degrees to one side, then rotate them to the other side. Move from the hips, keep the chest tall.

demo.sourceName: mobilitychick training exercise dab flow GIF

exercises.name: Glute Bridge March
exercises.how: Hold a glute bridge and lift one knee at a time toward your chest. Do not let the hips drop or tilt.
exercises.auditReason: Pattern is genuinely split: the anti-rotation/anti-tilt demand argues for 'core' or 'anti-rotation' while the bridge position argues for 'hinge' — worth a human call since it feeds recovery tracking.

exercises.name: Wall Angel
exercises.how: Back flat against the wall, slide your arms up and down keeping wrists and elbows touching. Keep the lower back close to the wall.

exercises.auditReason: Equipment vs movement: a Pallof is defined by resistance anchored to the side of the body, and a dumbbell held at the chest applies only a downward/forward load — with no cable and no bands on hand, this anti-rotation exercise cannot be produced at all.
exercises.how: Hold a light dumbbell out in front of your chest with both hands and stand still. Ribs down, resist letting it pull you forward.
exercises.name: Standing Pallof Hold

exercises.how: Jump straight up pulling your knees toward your chest, land softly. Bend the knees on landing to absorb it.
exercises.name: Tuck Jump
Lateral Shuffle
exercises.how: Stay low in a half squat and shuffle sideways a few steps each way. Keep the chest up and feet from crossing.
exercises.auditReason: Correctly described agility warm-up that fits pickleball; role/progression could also be argued as power/quality if it is run as a speed drill.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Chest-Supported Shrug
exercises.how: Chest on the incline bench, shrug the dumbbells up toward your ears. Pause a second at the top, no neck rolling.
exercises.auditReason: Single-joint scapular elevation is correctly 'isolation', but a catalog that treats shrugs as upper-back work may expect 'pull'; the incline chest support is achievable on eq-ea11007d.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Suitcase Hold
exercises.how: Hold the kettlebell at one side and stand tall for time. Do not let that shoulder drop or the torso lean.
Palms facing down, curl the dumbbells up keeping the elbows pinned to your sides. Go light, the wrists work hard here.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Curl
Dumbbell Farmer's Hold
exercises.how: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and stand tall for time. Shoulders back, ribs down.
Support yourself on the dip bars with straight arms and raise your knees to your chest. Keep shoulders pressed down, no swinging.
exercises.name: Dip Bar Knee Raise
Dip Bar Oblique Knee Raise
exercises.how: Supported on the dip bars, raise your knees toward one side, alternating sides slowly. No swinging or dropping fast.
exercises.auditReason: Correct as described, but note this is trunk rotation under bodyweight rather than anti-rotation, so back risk is moderate rather than low for an athlete prioritising lower-back resilience.

exercises.name: Tuck L-Sit
exercises.how: Support on the bars and hold both knees tucked to your chest. Push the shoulders down away from your ears.
Support yourself on the bars with straight arms and shrug your shoulders up and down. Small controlled range.
exercises.auditReason: NAME vs MOVEMENT: on dip bars the working action is scapular depression/elevation in a support hold, so 'shrug' is loosely descriptive; a name like 'Dip Bar Scapular Depression' would match the movement better.
exercises.name: Dip Bar Shoulder Shrug

exercises.how: Rear foot on the bench, drop the back knee toward the floor. Keep the front shin near vertical and torso upright.
exercises.name: Bench Bulgarian Split Squat

exercises.how: Hands on the bench set high, do push-ups, lowering the backrest a notch each round. Keep the body in one line throughout.
exercises.name: Bench Incline Push-up Ladder

exercises.how: Feet wide, toes out, hold the kettlebell between your legs and squat down. Keep the chest up and knees pushed out.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Sumo Squat

exercises.auditReason: Metadata: the movement is squat plus overhead press and a single pattern cannot represent both, so the push tag under-reports lower-body recovery cost.
exercises.how: Front squat two dumbbells, then drive up and press them overhead in one motion. Keep ribs down at lockout, no back arch.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Thruster

exercises.how: Lie on the floor and open the dumbbells wide with a slight elbow bend until the upper arms touch down. The floor caps the stretch.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Floor Fly

exercises.auditReason: Load-vs-purpose: the how-to calls for a 'very light' dumbbell but the minimum is 8 lb, which is well past cuff-prehab loading and puts the shoulder at loaded end-range external rotation.
exercises.name: Prone Dumbbell External Rotation
exercises.how: Lie face down on the bench, upper arm out at 90 degrees, rotate a very light dumbbell up. Slow, no momentum.

exercises.name: Dip Bar Tuck Hold Swing
exercises.auditReason: momentum-driven, contradicts the "no swinging" cue on every other dip-bar row, adds nothing over the knee raise
exercises.how: Support on the bars with knees tucked and gently swing the legs forward and back under control. Keep arms locked.
